title: Coding agent PR bodies: a hunk-anchored Tour at the head sha replaces the prose Changes / How to review
tldr: The coding agent's PR descriptions are hard for a human to consume: dense prose that never points at the code (see [#325](https://github.com/coreplanelabs/switchboard/pull/325)). This PR replaces the prose **Changes** / **How to review** sections of the PR-body template with a **Tour** — an ordered, reader-first walkthrough where each step is a heading naming the change, an explanation, and then a line permalink at the PR head that GitHub renders as embedded code — written by the agent that just made the change, so it costs no extra model call.
whatWhy: First piece of the "PRs consumable by humans" work (Tour in the body → skills provenance [#331](https://github.com/coreplanelabs/switchboard/pull/331) → the description as data with one renderer per surface ([features/pr-description.md](https://github.com/coreplanelabs/switchboard/blob/main/features/pr-description.md)) → typed skill events → optional meat reading diff → review-run panel). Modeled on Ramp Inspect's hunk-anchored Tour (`competitive-research/ramp-inspect/findings.md` #2, #8), with two improvements: GitHub is the renderer (a `blob/<40-char sha>/<path>#L<a>-L<b>` link inside a PR body renders as the code itself — no UI built), and each step leads with *what the change is* and *why*, so the reader knows what they are looking at before the hunk appears. The author writes it right after implementing because that is when it has the most context anyone will ever have about the change. This body itself was produced by the `PrDescription` pipeline from `src/core/testing/pr329.description.json` — the PR is the pipeline's golden test.

tour.title: The template — Tour replaces Changes and How to review
tour.description: The shared `PR_DESCRIPTION_TEMPLATE` (both coding prompts embed it). Every section is a `##` heading, the TL;DR included. The Tour bullet fixes the step shape — `### N. <what this change is>` heading → one paragraph → optional **Look for:** → permalink last — in reading order (entry point → core logic → tests → docs), anchors ≲25 lines, a `Remaining changes` catch-all, markdown structure over prose, and the repush rule: the sha comes from `git rev-parse HEAD` after pushing and the Tour is regenerated on every push that moves the head.
tour.lookFor: the ordering is explicit ("permalink to the hunk LAST"), and the sha rule says *full 40-char* — the one detail a model will economize on.

tour.title: Tests — written red first
tour.description: Four failed before the template change (`**Tour**` missing, the old sections present, no permalink shape, no repush rule). They pin: the six-section list; `**Changes**` / `**How to review**` gone from both prompts; every section a `##` heading with `## TL;DR` first; the exact permalink shape GitHub embeds; "reading order" + "Remaining changes"; the step order (heading, **Look for:**, "permalink to the hunk LAST", "headings for steps, bold labels"); `git rev-parse HEAD` + "every push that changes the head".

decisions.title: Author-written, not generated
decisions.rationale: Inspect generates its Tour with a second cheap model call at PR-open. Ours is written by the coding agent inside the same run: strictly more context, zero extra cost. The trade-off is that it depends on the agent following the template — covered by the `[agent]` criterion, not by code.

decisions.title: Heading → explanation → code, not code first
decisions.rationale: Inspect shows the hunk then the note. A reader who sees code before knowing what it is for has to read it twice; the heading names the change, the paragraph says why, and the permalink confirms it.

decisions.title: Full 40-char sha, spelled out
decisions.rationale: A branch ref renders as a bare link; the full sha always embeds. (Reviewer nit on the first push: unambiguous short shas do embed too — the full sha is still the safer instruction.)

decisions.title: Repush regeneration is in the template, not a post-step — for now
decisions.rationale: The agent already does the push; "update the PR body in the same step" is the smallest correct change. The proper fix is the data pipeline: anchors stored as (path, from, to) and rendered against the head sha, so a repush is a re-render — that is what `renderPrDescriptionMarkdown` does, and the roadmap item tracks wiring the agent to it.

decisions.title: Dropped "How to review" rather than keeping both
decisions.rationale: The Tour *is* the ordered review guide; two sections saying where to start would drift.

risks: Prompt-only change to `PR_DESCRIPTION_TEMPLATE`; no runtime code paths change. Blast radius: the shape of every PR body the coding agent opens from the next bot deploy. Existing PRs untouched. If the agent anchors badly (wrong lines after a rebase) the body degrades to a link that still opens the file — no worse than the prose it replaces.
